primary_work.title: BISCUIT: Causal Representation Learning from Binary Interactions

boundary: unknown binary-interaction target identifiability and action-conditioned affordance discovery are prior art; raw-language equivalence, residual semantic target partition, and denotation remain unidentified inside interaction-equivalence classes and under joint relabeling
counterexample: two semantic ontologies with identical complete action/state-conditioned binary interaction variables, transition laws, frame/action distributions, affordance maps, task behavior, and language-control statistics but different utterance equivalence, target partition, and denotation
surviving_rq: After recovering the strongest causal-variable and interaction-target partition identifiable from all legitimate non-language frames, actions, states, and transition mechanisms, can a preregistered raw-language observation law uniquely refine the remaining interaction-aliased blocks and jointly identify utterance equivalence, residual semantic target partition, and denotation while eliminating every joint recoding preserving the complete interactive process?
